topic.subject: science
topic.title: Light: mirrors and lenses
topic.scope: plane mirror image, concave and convex mirrors and lenses, real and virtual images, dispersion of white light

concepts.name: Rectilinear propagation of light and reflection

misconceptions.statement: Light travels only from the source to the object, not to the eye.
misconceptions.why: Students often focus on the light source as the active agent and ignore the role of the eye in receiving reflected light.
misconceptions.fix: We see objects because light reflects off them and enters our eyes.

probe.question: Why can you see a book in a dark room if you turn on a torch?
probe.wrong_answer: The torch light hits the book and stays there so the book becomes visible.

misconceptions.statement: A mirror adds something to the object to create an image.
misconceptions.why: Students perceive the image as a physical entity existing behind the mirror rather than a reflection of light.
misconceptions.fix: The image is just light rays reflecting off the mirror surface to our eyes, creating the appearance of an object behind it.

probe.question: Where does the image go when you move away from the mirror?
probe.wrong_answer: It stays behind the mirror waiting for me to come back.

misconceptions.statement: Concave mirrors always make objects look smaller.
misconceptions.why: Students often generalize their experience with the back of a spoon (convex) to all curved surfaces.
misconceptions.fix: Concave mirrors can make objects look larger or smaller depending on how close the object is to the mirror.

probe.question: What happens to your face if you look into a concave makeup mirror from very close?
probe.wrong_answer: It looks smaller than my actual face.

misconceptions.statement: A lens works by blocking some light to create an image.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the bending of light (refraction) with the blocking of light (shadows).
misconceptions.fix: Lenses change the direction of light rays by bending them as they pass through the glass.

probe.question: How does a magnifying glass make things look bigger?
probe.wrong_answer: It blocks the extra light around the edges so only the middle part is seen.

concepts.name: Real vs Virtual images and Dispersion

misconceptions.statement: A real image is one that is physically present on the screen.
misconceptions.why: Students interpret 'real' as a solid object rather than a collection of light rays focused at a point.
misconceptions.fix: A real image is formed where light rays actually meet on a screen, but it is still just light, not a physical object.

probe.question: If you touch the screen where a real image is projected, what will you feel?
probe.wrong_answer: I will feel the object that is being projected.

misconceptions.statement: A prism adds colors to white light.
misconceptions.why: Students see the colors coming out of the prism and assume the prism is the source of the color.
misconceptions.fix: White light is actually a mixture of many colors, and the prism just separates them.

probe.question: Where do the rainbow colors come from when white light passes through a prism?
probe.wrong_answer: The glass of the prism contains those colors and paints the light.
